headline: Intimate venues, eminent musicians
summary: Four extraordinary musicians. One extraordinary week. And music you won’t hear anywhere else.
intro: For ten days, exceptional musicians will be part of the fabric of our community. There will be opportunities to encounter them at rehearsals, conversations, discussions and performances — sometimes planned, sometimes spontaneous.

The Festival Quartet then takes its music on the road, with three Pay What You Can finale concerts designed to make this extraordinary music accessible throughout southwestern Nova Scotia. Featuring classics of chamber music repertoire by Haydn, Shostakovich, and Brahms and a special world premiere of this year's commissioned work only in Yarmouth.
afterword: Over the past ten days, the festival has travelled from Yarmouth to the Acadian communities of West Pubnico and Church Point. Audiences chose the music at kitchen parties, heard world-class musicians in museums and chapels, and listened in near-total darkness at the Ritchie Memorial Chapel at the Yarmouth Mountain Cemetery. If you were part of any of it, thank you.
Our belief remains the same: great music belongs here, not only in big cities, and it’s best shared as neighbours.
Thank you for making possible music that matters, right here, at home. We hope you’ll be with us again next year.
scheduleNote: The Festival Quartet also gave free storytelling concerts in schools, sat in with the local orchestra at Yarmouth High School, and held an open rehearsal at the Yarmouth Regional Hospital.

events.title: Classical Kitchen Party I
description: Meet the festival quartet and hear them play works by your favorite composers. Light refreshments will be served. Very limited seating - exact location in town (Yarmouth) will be disclosed after tickets are purchased.
*What to expect*
- Music in a private, welcoming home setting
- Conversation and connection with the musicians — ask questions, hear the stories behind the music, and even choose what the musicians play!
- A relaxed atmosphere that blends the warmth of a Nova Scotian kitchen party with the beauty of chamber music
- Light refreshments will be served

The most unique part of the evening is that you get to choose the program. Festival Artistic Director and violist David Yang will bring a stack of string quartets followed by lively voting from the attendees on which composer they want the musicians to play: it's sight reading as a contact sport!

events.title: Night Music: Music in the Dark
description: Chamber music performed by the Festival Quartet in near-darkness! Lowered visual stimulation increases aural sensitivity for a truly memorable experience.

An experience unlike any other festival concert. Imagine entering a beautiful Gothic mortuary chapel. The lights go down. The quartet begins to play. There is almost nothing to see. The music has not been announced beforehand. With visual stimulation deliberately reduced, your ears become more sensitive to every sound, every silence, every breath and every movement of the music.

events.title: Grand Finale in Yarmouth
description: Say farewell to the 2026 festival with this concert at Holy Trinity Church in Yarmouth with a program of works by Josef Haydn, Dmitri Shostakovich, Johannes Brahms and a world premiere for choir and string quartet, composed by our 2026 Composer in Residence, Gary Ewer. The new work, Songs From the Sea-Bound Coast, will be performed by Yarmouth's Aurora Singers conducted by Lan Day.
Celebrate with the musicians after the concert at the reception held in the parish hall.
